reviewers.interpretation_notes: PRIMARY COUNT: P=4, C=4, U=0. Rung: Supported. (1) Integrated Service Package 'Improved Accessibility - Active Pathway Snow Removal and Sidewalk Repair'. Source: FCS03158 Attachment 2, pp. 27 and 43-44, DocumentId 278877 (re-listed as 280346). Listed on the City Council agenda of 2025-11-24, item 7.2. Its text states $9,938K of 2026 incremental operating cost and 35.2 FTEs, a '$2.11 million one-time capital investment', and '$1.60 million to prioritize SNIC efforts in socially vulnerable areas'. (2) Standalone Service Package 'Parking Ban Enforcement Strategies and Resource Allocation'. Source: the same Attachment 2, pp. 25 and 34, same item. It states $100K ongoing for contracted towing during parking bans. Its text says it 'improves service levels for snow and ice control' and supports 'street blading for snow removal'. This is my borderline inclusion. (3) The 'Well Maintained City' service package. Source: CO03513 Attachment 9 (DocumentId 304812; 303388 in the 2026-08-22 capture by the order of the listing) and the report (304803/303379). Listed under item 7.1 of the Community and Public Services Committee meeting of 2026-08-31. The agenda was published by 2026-08-22 per the Internet Archive capture, and the draft was before the Agenda Review Committee on 2026-08-18. It states 'approximately $23.6 million annually in ongoing operating and $11.5 million in one-time capital'. It proposes eight-day residential blading and a Priority 1 Cycle Crew, among other changes. (4) The set of optional enhancements in CO03513 Attachment 10 (304813/303389), presented separately from the package 'to supplement' it. It contains 24 items, each with an estimated ongoing and/or one-time cost. I counted it once because it is not a service package. A reader who folds it into CO03513 gets P=3. The rung does not depend on items 2 or 4: items 1 and 3 alone give C=2. NOT COUNTED: (a) the Winter/Summer Temporary Assignment to Permanent Positions package, $1,777K (Attachment 2, pp. 45-46). It is a workforce and benefits conversion that names snow and ice only as one service it supports, not a change to snow service. (b) CS03123 / Bylaw 21283 (Community and Public Services Committee, 2026-01-19, item 7.1). I could not read it. Taproot reports it as a cut to the parking-ban fine from $250 to $150, with costed early-payment options. That is a fine change, not a snow-service change. Even if it were counted as U, it could not move the primary rung, because C is already at least 2. Motions are not counted: 2025-08-11 item 7.3, notice 2026-01-19 item 11.1, 2026-03-17 items 10.3 and 10.4, and the 2026-08-31 motions. Each package has one cost: the incremental figure its own text states. No proposal in the window establishes an excess over an identified approved budget. ALTERNATIVES: (i) Considered by a body by 2026-08-27. Items 1 and 2 count: Council dealt with item 7.2 on 2025-11-24/25 (presentations, questions, a private session and a postponement motion) and again on 2025-12-01 to 12-04. Items 3 and 4 do not: their first meeting was 2026-08-31. P=2, C=2, U=0: Supported. If the parking-ban package is excluded, C=1 and the rung is Partially supported, so this result depends on that classification. (ii) Window to 2026-10-02. Under agenda placement P=4, C=4: Supported. Under considered-by, P=4, C=4: Supported, because the committee dealt with item 7.1 on 2026-08-31 and Council dealt with item 7.9 on 2026-09-08 without debate. (iii) Pre-election start, 2025-01-01. CO03079 (2025-08-11, item 7.3; Options 2-4 costed) is the earlier version of package 1, and CS02945 (2025-06-16, unread) is the earlier version of package 2, so each counts once. P=4, C=4: Supported. (iv) City Council alone. Items 1 and 2 were on the 2025-11-24 Council agenda. CO03513 first reached a Council agenda on 2026-09-08, behind a committee report, so after the comment date. P=2, C=2: Supported; Partially supported if package 2 is excluded. (v) Separately costed options. Package 1 = 1, package 2 = 1, the Well Maintained City package = 1 (no costed sub-options), and the Attachment 10 enhancements = 24. C=27: Supported. (vi) Stricter cost reading, which requires an approved figure plus the increase against it. No proposal in the window states the approved snow and ice budget. Attachment 2 gives only 'incremental' and 'New Budget' columns. CO03513 states no baseline, and the FCS03158 report says only that unfunded packages 'would require an approved Council amendment to add to the budget'. P=4, C=0, U=0: Contradicted. With the pre-election start, CO03079 states 'The total budget for SNIC is $67 million/year' and 'Funding for these scenarios does not exist within the current budget', giving C=1: Partially supported. (vii) Exactly two. P=C=4: Partially supported. The result is Supported only if the enhancements are folded in and the parking-ban package is excluded. The finding is therefore definition-sensitive under (vi), (vii) and, depending on how package 2 is classified, (i) and (iv). A reader-facing 'already put' should name the agenda-placement rule. Separately, the 'Well Maintained City' package was 'presented here for information ahead of formal presentation during 2027-2030 budget deliberations'. Packages 1 and 2 were labelled 'Council Directed', meaning Administration prepared them because a committee or Council motion required it. Under the brief's definition both count as Administration proposals.

Under the primary rule, a proposal is counted when its first published agenda lists it, even if the meeting is later. I count the Fall 2025 Improved Accessibility service package once, whether appearing first in CO03079 or as its updated answer in FCS03158, and the Well Maintained City package once. The 24 optional enhancements in CO03513 Attachment 10 are not separate primary service packages. Primary count: P=2, C=2, U=0; Supported. Alternative timing rule, considered by a body by 2026-08-27: P=1, C=1, U=0; Partially supported, because CO03513 was considered on 2026-08-31. Alternative window through 2026-10-02: P=2, C=2, U=0; Supported under agenda placement, and P=2, C=2, U=0; Supported under the considered-by-body rule. Pre-election start 2025-01-01: P=2, C=2, U=0; Supported; CO03079 and its later budget package are counted once. Council alone, primary timing: P=1, C=1, U=0; Partially supported; CO03513 was first before a committee by the comment date, and Council's agenda listing was later. Separately costed options: P=27, C=27, U=0; Supported, counting the 24 CO03513 enhancements and the three costed CO03079 options, with the later FCS03158 package not counted again. Stricter cost reading requiring the text to establish excess over an identified approved budget: P=2, C=1, U=0; Partially supported. The CO03513 package states costs but not an approved budget baseline and increase against it; the FCS03158 package is expressly unfunded. Exactly-two rule: P=2, C=2, U=0; Supported. The reader-facing answer must identify the agenda-placement timing rule; under the considered-by-body timing rule the answer is Partially supported.

Primary count: P=3, C=3, U=0; Supported. I count the November 2025 parking-ban towing and active-pathway packages, plus the Well Maintained City package listed for the 2026-08-31 committee meeting. I group the 24 dependent enhancements in CO03513 Attachment 10 with that presentation under the primary package unit; they are separately costed options under the alternative unit. I exclude the November 2025 Winter/Summer Temporary Assignment package: it changes employment status across several services but specifies no change to snow and ice control service or operations. The 2026-08-31 agenda's reported 2026-08-22 archive capture is the basis for counting Well Maintained City by the comment date; I could not independently retrieve that capture. Required alternatives, changing only the named rule: considered by a body by 2026-08-27, P=2/C=2/U=0, Supported; window through 2026-10-02, P=3/C=3/U=0, Supported; start at 2025-01-01, P=3/C=3/U=0 after deduplicating the earlier versions of the two Fall 2025 packages, Supported; City Council alone, P=2/C=2/U=0, Supported; separately costed options, P=27/C=27/U=0 if all 24 items in Attachment 10 are treated as snow and ice enhancements, Supported; cost exceeding an explicitly identified approved budget, P=3/C=0/U=0, Contradicted because none of the three counted package texts gives both an approved snow-service budget figure and its increase against that figure; exactly two, P=3/C=3/U=0, Partially supported because a third costed package is listed. The stricter cost and exact-count readings change the rung. 'Already asked' here means placed on a published agenda: the Well Maintained City item was not considered by the committee until 2026-08-31. Neither placement nor consideration establishes approval or expenditure.

round2_positions.interpretation_notes: Final position: Supported, unchanged from round 1. PRIMARY (agenda placement; Council or committee; one count per service package; cost stated): P=3, C=3, U=0. (A) Integrated service package 'Improved Accessibility - Active Pathway Snow Removal and Sidewalk Repair'. FCS03158 Attachment 2, DocumentId 278877 (re-listed as 280346), pp. 27, 43-44. City Council agenda 2025-11-24, item 7.2 (an addendum item, added at adoption in minutes item 1.4; exact publication day not fixed, latest possible date 2025-11-24). First dealt with by Council 2025-11-25 (presentations and questions under items 7.1-7.3 together). Proposes raising SNIC priority in socially vulnerable areas, plus enforcement and sidewalk repair. Stated cost: 'a $2.11 million one-time capital investment, an annual ongoing operating increase of $1.60 million to prioritize SNIC efforts ... $1.64 million to enforcement services, as well as $4.59 million for proactive Sidewalk Maintenance repairs'; table: 2026 New Budget $9,938K, 35.2 FTEs. Establishes an excess over an identified approved budget: no. (B) Standalone service package 'Parking Ban Enforcement Strategies and Resource Allocation'. Same attachment, pp. 25, 34; same agenda and the same first-dealt date. Proposes contracted towing during parking bans; $100K ongoing in 2026. Its text says it 'improves service levels for snow and ice control'. Excess over an approved budget: no. Counting B is a judgement on a borderline case: it continues towing first funded one-time from 2025 Council contingency, and its lead branch is Community Standards. (C) 'Well Maintained City' service package. CO03513 Attachment 9, DocumentId 304812, and report 304803. CPSC 2026-08-31, item 7.1. First on a published agenda by 2026-08-22 per the archive capture the brief identifies (I have not verified it independently); first dealt with by the committee 2026-08-31. Proposes an eight-day residential blading window, a Priority 1 Cycle Crew, an event snow team, and enforcement. Stated cost: 'approximately $23.6 million in ongoing operating investment and $11.5 million in one-time capital funding', which also covers non-snow work (turf, sweeping, graffiti, inspections). Excess over an approved budget: no. The rung is robust to losing either B or C, but not both. Not counted: the C409L policy recommendation (the report says it needs 'no additional budget'); the 2026-27 operational changes the report says are within the current budget; the Winter/Summer positions package (no stated snow service change); and the $2.1M fleet inflation adjustment in FCS03158 (maintains service, does not change it). Counting the first two would raise P but not C or U. Attachment 10's 24 optional enhancements are not a separately presented service package, so they belong under the alternative unit. The commenter was probably thinking of CO03513 (the package plus its enhancements). Under the primary unit that is one proposal, so the verdict reaches two partly through the Fall 2025 packages. The verdict is about the proposition as defined, not the commenter's referent. ALTERNATIVES (one rule changed at a time): considered by a body by 2026-08-27: A and B considered by Council 2025-11-25; P=2, C=2, U=0, Supported (Partially supported if B is excluded, which is luna's result). Window to 2026-10-02: P=3, C=3, U=0, Supported under both timing rules (the 2026-08-31 motions requesting future packages are motions, not proposals). Pre-election start 2025-01-01: CO03079 (CPSC 2025-08-11 item 7.3) is counted once with A as an earlier version of Option 3, and CS02945 once with B; P=3, C=3, U=0, Supported, bounded to the record carried. City Council alone: A and B on Council's 2025-11-24 agenda; Well Maintained City reached Council only on 2026-09-08; P=2, C=2, U=0, Supported (Partially supported without B). Separately costed options: 24 (Attachment 10) + 3 packages = P=27, C=27, U=0, Supported; 24 are counted by the attachment's title, and on my reading items 19, 20 and 22 (catch basins, sweeping flushers) are not snow service changes. Stricter cost reading: no counted text in the window states an approved snow and ice budget and the increase against it; P=3, C=0, U=0, Contradicted. In this case that rung means only 'no baseline stated in the text'. It does not mean no new money was asked, because each package is expressly incremental or unfunded. The only stated baseline, CO03079's '$67 million/year' (2025), sits outside the primary window. Exactly two: C=3, Partially supported. The finding is DEFINITION-SENSITIVE: the stricter cost reading and the exactly-two rule each change the rung, and the story must say so beside the verdict. Under my count the two timing rules give the same rung. Even so, any reader-facing 'already put' should name the agenda-placement rule, because the third package had only been placed on an agenda, not considered, by 2026-08-27. Framing note (not material): the ladder's Contradicted wording ('what had been put states no new spending') misdescribes the strict-reading result here, and the story should not use that wording. The brief assigns no verdict on the four parked claims. For context only, CO03513 costs 'Calcium Chloride System Upgrades' at $2.5M ongoing and $4.4M one-time, and none of the four 2026-08-31 committee motions names calcium chloride.

Verdict: Supported under the primary readings. Among the identified documents, P=3, C=3, U=0: (1) Parking Ban Enforcement Strategies and Resource Allocation, DocumentId 278877, states $100,000 ongoing in 2026 for contracted towing during parking bans; (2) Improved Accessibility - Active Pathway Snow Removal and Sidewalk Repair, DocumentId 278877, states new spending, including a $2.11 million one-time capital investment and 2026 operating amounts that conflict internally: the component description totals $7.83 million ($1.60M + $1.64M + $4.59M), while the table totals $9.938 million; (3) Well Maintained City, DocumentId 304812, describes winter service changes and states approximately $23.6 million ongoing operating and $11.5 million one-time capital for a broader winter and complementary seasonal package. The 24 enhancements in Attachment 10 are counted as separately costed options under the alternative unit, not as another primary service package. The August 31, 2026 committee agenda was captured by the Internet Archive on August 22, before the comment date; the committee did not consider the item until August 31. Required alternatives: considered-by-body timing through 2026-08-27: P=2, C=2, U=0, Supported. Window through 2026-10-02: identified P=3, C=3, U=0, Supported under either timing rule, since the committee considered CO03513 on August 31. Pre-election start: CO03079 is an earlier version of the active-pathway package, counted once; the identified proposals still give P at least 3, C at least 3, U=0, Supported, but the exact total is not established by the supplied meeting records. Council alone: P=2, C=2, U=0, Supported; CO03513 first reached Council after the comment date. Separately costed options: identified P=27, C=27, U=0, Supported (two Fall 2025 packages, the Well Maintained City package, and 24 Attachment 10 options). Stricter cost reading requiring an identified approved budget and stated increase: P=3, C=0, U=0, Contradicted; the counted proposal texts do not establish that comparison. Exactly-two rule: identified P=3, C=3, U=0, Partially supported. These changes make the result definition-sensitive. The primary result establishes published agenda placement under the brief's definition; it does not establish that Council approved funding or that the Well Maintained City package had been formally submitted for a budget decision. The exact total may be higher because the supplied records do not constitute a complete search of every agenda in every required window.

Primary agenda-placement count: P=3, C=3, U=0; Supported. Count once each: (1) Improved Accessibility - Active Pathway Snow Removal and Sidewalk Repair, FCS03158 Attachment 2, DocumentId 278877, Council item 7.2 on 2025-11-24; (2) Parking Ban Enforcement Strategies and Resource Allocation, the same attachment and item; and (3) Well Maintained City, CO03513 report DocumentId 304803 and Attachment 9 DocumentId 304812, committee item 7.1 on the agenda captured 2026-08-22. For the November agenda, the first publication day is unknown; 2025-11-24 is the latest possible day. The first two were dealt with by Council on 2025-11-24/25, then postponed to its 2025-12-01 budget meeting. The third was first dealt with by the committee on 2026-08-31; Council dealt with the policy report on 2026-09-08. The 2026 optional enhancements in Attachment 10 are separately costed options under the alternative unit, not another primary service package. The Winter/Summer positions package states no specific change to snow service. Required alternatives, holding other primary choices fixed: considered by a body by 2026-08-27, P=2, C=2, U=0, Supported; window through 2026-10-02, P=3, C=3, U=0, Supported under either timing rule; pre-election start 2025-01-01, P=3, C=3, U=0, Supported, counting CO03079 and its updated Fall 2025 package once; City Council alone by the comment date, P=2, C=2, U=0, Supported; separately costed options, P=27, C=27, U=0, Supported, counting the two Fall 2025 packages, Well Maintained City and 24 listed enhancements without duplicating the earlier CO03079 options; stricter cost test requiring an identified approved figure and a stated increase against it, P=3, C=0, U=0, Contradicted; exactly two, P=3, C=3, U=0, Partially supported. The finding is definition-sensitive to the stricter cost and exact-count readings. Every reader-facing use of 'already put' or 'already asked' must say it means placed on a published agenda by August 27. These are proposed costs, not spending approvals or actual spending. The Well Maintained City figures cover a broader seasonal package, not snow clearing alone. Its future formal budget presentation and the policy's no-additional-budget approval are separate matters.
